## Design

### 2026-10-07 — Day 1 — Schematic & PCB

**3h**

Day 1 — Schematic & PCB
Today I started my PCB project using KiCad. I first installed and added the required symbol and footprint libraries from the provided Care Package so that I could use the project's custom components.
I then created the complete schematic for the project. I added the XIAO ESP32-C3 as the main microcontroller, along with the required power connections, buttons, OLED connector, MPU6050 connector, and DHT11 sensor. I connected the components according to the project design and used net labels to keep the schematic organized and reduce unnecessary wiring.
After completing the schematic, I assigned the appropriate footprints to the components. This allowed the schematic components to have their corresponding physical representations on the PCB.
Finally, I updated the PCB from the completed schematic and started working with the physical PCB layout. This helped me understand how the electrical connections in a schematic are transferred into an actual PCB design.
Today I learned how to create and organize a schematic, use custom libraries, connect components using nets, assign footprints, and update a PCB from a schematic. This gave me a much better understanding of the overall PCB design workflow in KiCad.
